provider: TheHost.ua KeepData — 10 TB flat with traffic included, WebDAV/SFTP/Samba, the best Western-facing $/TB in the set

free_tier.stated: 25 GB / 100 GB / 500 GB / 1 TB / 10 TB / 50 TB. 10 TB = $59.48/mo, or $642.34/yr (10 % discount), or $1,141.90 for 2 years (20 %). Also sold in UAH and EUR on the same table (2,499 ₴ / €49.98 / $59.48 per month for 10 TB). Inodes: 1,000 K at 10 TB. 7-day free trial on every tier.

egress.terms: Included and unmetered — the traffic row reads simply «Traffic», with access speed «10 Gbit/s», and there is no meter, overage rate or traffic pack anywhere on the page. This is a dedicated-rail storage product, not metered object storage.

tooling: FTP, FTPS, SFTP, WebDAV (mounts as a network drive on Windows/macOS), plus BorgBackup / Restic / rsync / rclone over SFTP. Double redundancy across two physical datacentres in different cities. Auto-delete rules for camera/stream ingest.
chaining: Sizing is by purchased volume, so 5 TB → 2× and 20 TB → 2× the 10 TB plan, both at the same per-TB rate. No account multiplication needed.
limits_note: Not S3 — no bucket API, no presigned URLs, so the client's CDN/CF fronting has to go through WebDAV or an rclone `serve` layer. Inode ceilings matter for a 20 TiB corpus of small files: 1,000 K inodes at 10 TB is 1 M files, which a dataset archive of many small parquet/JSON shards will exhaust long before 10 TB. Per-file size not published on the pricing page.
reliability_note: Ukrainian operator (Kyiv), billing in UAH/EUR/USD with card. The 10 Gbit/s claim and the double-redundancy claim are the vendor's own and were not independently benchmarked here — treat throughput as unverified. The 7-day trial is real and is the right way to test before committing 20 TiB.

extras.price_verbatim: $5.95/TB/mo at 10 TB ($59.48/mo) and identically at 50 TB ($297.48/mo) — flat rate, unmetered traffic, no volume discount at either end. Tier ladder is 25 GB / 100 GB / 500 GB / 1 TB / 10 TB / 50 TB, so there is NO 5 TB SKU: 5 TB means buying 5× the 1 TB plan ($64.15/mo = $12.83/TB/mo, poor) or 1× the 10 TB plan and using half of it ($5.95/TB/mo paid, $11.90/TB/mo effectively). 20 TB = 2× the 10 TB plan at $119/mo (derived; confirm they allow a second unit). At 1 TB the rate is $12.83/TB/mo, so buying the 10 TB tier is 2.16× cheaper per terabyte than buying the 1 TB tier.
